Actual pilot here, and I can tell you (almost) exactly what happened based on this video/audio alone.

Pilot was flying in IMC (instrument meteorological conditions, which means you can't see anything and must rely on your instruments). The pilot became spatially disoriented. This is exceptionally common, and is the reason why it's called instrument meteorological conditions. Basically your inner ear cannot keep long-term track of your position and movement without visual feedback (seeing the ground). The plane went into a steep dive, over-stressed and broke up in mid-air.

No missile.

Why did the pilot become spatially disoriented? Possible reasons:

  • Maybe he thought he turned on the auto-pilot but didn't.
  • Maybe the autopilot malfunctioned and he didn't notice.
  • Maybe the autopilot was not set correctly (altitude set very low), but many autopilots have limit detection so this is unlikely.
  • Maybe the pilot was inexperienced or not properly trained for IMC flight.
  • Maybe there was an instrument failure and the pilot didn't pick up on it in time.
  • Maybe the pilot was otherwise incapacitated.
